The county page has no infobox area; the modern comarca of Pallars Sobirà is 1,378 km2 (comarca page), a ratio of 2.2 that is the grid's 252 km2 cell size rather than a wrong shape. Jussà's shape (7 cells) shares no cell with it. The page is silent on the borders and on Vall d'Aran, Alt Àneu and Ribagorza.

ledger.note: 1011: Pallars is divided and William II receives Pallars Sobirà. 'In 1011, Sunyer of Pallars died and by his testament his county was divided between his sons'; 'the younger, William II, receiving Pallars Sobirà', which 'comprised the original heartland of the county of Pallars'. The other son took Pallars Jussà.

ledger.note: 1199: the county passes to a woman and then to Comminges. 'By 1199, Pallars Sobirà was inherited by a woman, Guillelma', who 'sold her county to her husband, Roger of Comminges, and retired to a convent' (undated); the list then runs Roger I 1229-1240. No land changes hands.

1487: the Crown takes the county. Hugh Roger III 'lost his County to the Crown in 1487 after being defeated in the War and subsequent rebellions'. The page says 'the Crown' without naming it; the Crown of Aragon is the reading.

notes:
Cliopatria's row (1040-1201, two shapes of the same 12 cells) covers a county that the page lists from 1011 (the partition of Pallars between Sunyer's sons) to 1487 (confiscated by 'the Crown' from Hugh Roger III), so keyframes pallars-sobira_1011 and _1202 carry the Cliopatria shape back to 1011 and forward to 1486; both are unverified (page budget, and the page is silent on borders). The Wikipedia field of Cliopatria and its Wikidata id Q12719 point to the modern comarca 'Pallars Sobirà'; the county has its own article 'County of Pallars Sobirà', which this dossier reads.
Not settled (page silent): the county's capital (the pages name only Segur for Jussà and Sort for the comarca); vassalage to Barcelona, Urgell, Aragon or Toulouse (the page has only 'in alliance with Ermengol III of Urgell'); Vall d'Aran, Alt Àneu, Ribagorza; the war of 1487 (its name and years); the infobox. The page notes (undated) that Raymond IV of Pallars Jussà 'lost most of his fortresses, including his capital, Segur, to Sobirà', a gain that would be Sobirà's from county-of-pallars-jussa but has no year, so it is not in the ledger; Jussà itself 'passed to the County of Barcelona in 1192'.
Counterparts: county-of-pallars (undivided Pallars, another part of eu-12) and county-of-pallars-jussa, crown-of-aragon. Page budget (1-2): County of Pallars Sobirà, Pallars Sobirà (the comarca, thin).
